newsitem.title: USA: Ecuador to set stage for EMETEL sale in 90 days.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador to set stage for EMETEL sale in 90 days.

text.p: Laws for the privatization of EMETEL, Ecuador's state-owned telephone company, will be enacted in the Congress within 90 days, Danilo Carrera, president of Ecuador's Monetary Board, said on Reuters Financial Television Tuesday.

The sale of EMETEL is part of President Fabian Alarcon's economic plan to raise revenues, which, along with spending cuts, is aimed at cutting the fiscal deficit to 2.5 percent of gross domestic product from the current 6.6 percent.

Carrera said the government must find alternatives to the extremely unpopular measures of raising gasoline and electricity rates, which contributed to the ouster of former president Abdala Bucaram from office last month.
Carrera expressed optimism that Ecuador's economic crisis has bottomed out, projecting 3.5 percent growth for this year and 4.0 percent for 1998.

The new Ecuadorean government will not be seeking money from the International Monetary Fund, whose officials arrived in Quito Monday night. Instead, it hopes to seek approval for its economic plan, Carrera said.
